summary: @onereach/webform preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute opaque obfuscated payload
details: package.json sets scripts.preinstall to `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated with obfuscator.io _0x identifiers and, at npm install time, constructs a URL of the form https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<VER>/<archive>.zip, downloads a Bun runtime archive, unzips it to a temporary directory, marks the binary executable, and then invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with an obfuscator.io shuffled numeric string array (n7gIxM), hex-prefixed identifiers, and a rotation function — its body is not human-readable and it is not referenced from any file under src/. The file name is unrelated to the package's stated Vue webform purpose. The CHANGELOG's last entry is 0.3.1 (2021-07-05) with no mention of Bun, math_init, or a preinstall step, while the published 0.3.15 tarball ships setup.mjs and math_init.js at the root with no `files` allowlist in package.json. The alternate-runtime path (executing the obfuscated bundle under a freshly downloaded Bun rather than Node) is structured to evade Node-based static inspection of the code that actually runs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
